places.name: The Boulevard du Temple
places.today: Still the Boulevard du Temple; its row of popular theatres, the 'Boulevard du Crime', was pulled down in 1862.

tagline.text: Boulevard of theatres, showmen and crowds, Little Gavroche's favourite haunt.

places.name: The house in the Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire
places.today: The street keeps its name, in the 3rd arrondissement near the Filles du Calvaire métro.

tagline.text: M. Gillenormand's old house at No. 6, in the Marais, where he lives with his daughter and his grandson.
Gillenormand's house, which Marius leaves after the quarrel over his father.
Gillenormand's house, where Marius is carried home from the barricade.
The Gillenormand house, where the wedding is celebrated and Marius and Cosette make their home.

places.name: Madame de T.'s salon, Rue Férou
places.today: The Rue Férou runs between the Place Saint-Sulpice and the Luxembourg.

tagline.text: Ultra-Royalist salon near Saint-Sulpice where Gillenormand reigns and brings the boy Marius.

places.name: Vernon
places.today: A town in the Eure, on the Seine about 75 km downstream of Paris.

tagline.text: Small town on the Seine in Normandy where a scarred half-pay colonel grows flowers.
Where Colonel Pontmercy dies, and where he is buried behind the church.

places.name: The Café Musain
places.today: Long gone; the old Place Saint-Michel lay near where the Boulevard Saint-Michel now meets the Rue Soufflot.

tagline.text: Little café near the Panthéon whose back room shelters the Friends of the A.B.C.
Café where Enjolras sends his friends out to sound the fighting men of Paris.

places.name: Corinthe
places.today: The Rue de la Chanvrerie vanished when the Rue Rambuteau was cut through under Louis-Philippe; Corinthe stood near today's Rue Mondétour.

tagline.text: Wine-shop near the Halles where the Friends of the A.B.C. also gather.
Father Hucheloup's old wine-shop in the Rue de la Chanvrerie, kept now by his widow.
Wine-shop at the heart of the barricade, its upstairs windows turned into loopholes.

places.name: The hôtel de la Porte-Saint-Jacques
places.today: The Rue Saint-Jacques, near the Panthéon, 5th arrondissement.

tagline.text: Students' lodging-house where Courfeyrac takes in the homeless Marius.

places.name: The house in the Rue de l'Ouest
places.today: This Rue de l'Ouest became part of the Rue d'Assas.

tagline.text: Quiet street along the western side of the Luxembourg.
Modest house where M. Leblanc and his daughter live, until they leave it without an address.
One of Jean Valjean's two spare lodgings, kept apart from the Rue Plumet house.

places.name: M. Mabeuf's cottage at Austerlitz
places.today: The old village of Austerlitz lay off the Boulevard de l'Hôpital, 13th arrondissement.

tagline.text: Little house and garden near the Salpêtrière where the ruined churchwarden lives with Mother Plutarque.

places.name: The Rue Mouffetard
places.today: Still the Rue Mouffetard, 5th arrondissement.

tagline.text: Old market street climbing the slope of the Left Bank.
Snowy street where Marius shadows Jondrette on his errands.

places.name: La Force prison
places.today: Demolished in 1845; it stood between the Rue Pavée and the Rue Malher, 4th arrondissement.

tagline.text: Prison in the Marais where talk of the underworld circulates.
Prison where Gavroche's father is held after the Gorbeau arrests.
Prison from whose roofs Brujon, Gueulemer and Thénardier break out on a stormy night.

places.name: Saint-Lazare prison
places.today: Demolished in the 1930s; its site is by the Rue du Faubourg-Saint-Denis, 10th arrondissement.

tagline.text: Women's prison where Gavroche's mother is held.

places.name: The Madelonettes
places.today: Demolished in 1866; it stood on the Rue des Fontaines-du-Temple, 3rd arrondissement.

tagline.text: Prison where Gavroche's sisters are held.

places.name: The Barrière du Maine
places.today: The gate stood near today's Avenue du Maine, by Montparnasse.

tagline.text: Gate in the city wall where Grantaire is sent to sound out the workmen.
City gate where Valjean and Cosette watch the chain-gang pass at dawn.

places.name: The Lark's meadow
places.today: Built over; the 'Champ de l'Alouette' lay near the Rue Corvisart, 13th arrondissement.

tagline.text: Lonely field by the little river Bièvre, near the Gobelins, where Marius comes to dream.
Field where Éponine finds Marius with an address to give him.

places.name: The house in the Rue Plumet
places.today: The Rue Plumet is now the Rue Oudinot, 7th arrondissement; the house's back door opened on the Rue de Babylone.

tagline.text: Street in the Faubourg Saint-Germain named in a prisoner's note: 'a gate on a garden'.
Secluded house and wild garden where Jean Valjean lives with Cosette and Toussaint.
Garden by the railings where Marius and Cosette first speak.
House that Thénardier's gang comes to rob, and Éponine turns them away.
House that Marius finds shut up and empty.

places.name: The Rue de l'Homme Armé
places.today: Swallowed by the Rue des Archives, between the Rue des Blancs-Manteaux and the Rue Sainte-Croix-de-la-Bretonnerie.

tagline.text: Narrow Marais street where Valjean keeps a second spare lodging.
No. 7, where Valjean moves Cosette and Toussaint on 4 June 1832.
Valjean's lodging, empty now of Cosette.

places.name: The Place de la Bastille
places.today: The July Column, raised in 1840, now stands in the middle of the square.

tagline.text: Square on the site of the old fortress, gateway to the Faubourg Saint-Antoine.
Square where the people of the faubourg join General Lamarque's funeral procession.

places.name: The elephant of the Bastille
places.today: Demolished in 1846; the July Column stands beside its site.

tagline.text: Huge plaster model of Napoleon's unbuilt fountain, rotting in a corner of the square; Gavroche lives inside it.

places.name: The Faubourg du Temple
places.today: The Rue du Faubourg-du-Temple, 10th and 11th arrondissements.

tagline.text: Where one of the two great barricades of June 1848 stood, at the canal.

places.name: Courfeyrac's lodging, Rue de la Verrerie
places.today: Still the Rue de la Verrerie, 4th arrondissement.

tagline.text: Street near the Hôtel de Ville where Courfeyrac lodges and takes Marius in.
No. 16: the address Marius scratches on Cosette's garden wall.

places.name: The Rue de Thorigny
places.today: The Musée Picasso is in this street, 3rd arrondissement.

tagline.text: Marais street where four old gossips howl at Gavroche.

places.name: The Marché Saint-Jean
places.today: Gone; it lay where the Rue de la Verrerie meets the Rue du Bourg-Tibourg.

tagline.text: Old market square behind the Hôtel de Ville.
Square where Gavroche joins Enjolras's armed band.

places.name: The Rue des Billettes
places.today: Now part of the Rue des Archives.

tagline.text: Marais street where a tall grey-haired stranger joins the marching band.

places.name: Saint-Merry
places.today: The church of Saint-Merri, by the Centre Pompidou.

tagline.text: Church whose tocsin sounds through the night of 5 June.

places.name: Saint-Eustache
places.today: The church of Saint-Eustache, beside the Forum des Halles.

tagline.text: Great church beside the Halles.

places.name: The barricade of the Rue de la Chanvrerie
places.today: The street disappeared when the Rue Rambuteau was cut through under Louis-Philippe.

tagline.text: Barricade near the Halles where Marius's friends await him.
Barricade thrown across the Rue de la Chanvrerie from paving-stones, casks and an overturned omnibus.
The barricade, taken by the troops on 6 June.

places.name: The Royal Printing Establishment
places.today: The Hôtel de Rohan, Rue Vieille-du-Temple, now part of the National Archives.

tagline.text: Printing-house in the Marais whose National Guard post fires blindly at Gavroche's handcart.

places.name: The sewers of Paris
places.today: The Paris sewers can be visited from the Quai d'Orsay.

tagline.text: Lutetia, the city of mud: the network of galleries beneath Paris.
Dark labyrinth under the Right Bank where Valjean wanders with Marius on his back.

places.name: The outlet of the Grand Sewer
places.today: Near today's Place de l'Alma; the Pont de l'Alma was built in 1856.

tagline.text: Locked sewer grating on the deserted right bank, beyond the Pont des Invalides.
Where the Grand Sewer meets the Seine, between the Pont de Jéna and the Pont des Invalides, barred by a locked grating.

places.name: The fontis
places.today: The old stone sewer here was rebuilt in 1836.

tagline.text: A sewer quagmire, where the paving has given way over quicksand.
Quicksand under the old sewer of the Faubourg Saint-Honoré, swollen by the rain.

places.name: The Pont au Change
places.today: Rebuilt in 1860, between the Châtelet and the Île de la Cité.

tagline.text: Bridge by the Châtelet, at the heart of the old city.

places.name: The Pont Notre-Dame
places.today: Rebuilt in 1853 and again in 1919, between the Hôtel de Ville and the Île de la Cité.

tagline.text: Bridge by the Place du Châtelet, where the Seine runs in a rapid between the piles; here Javert's last walk ends.

places.name: The Blaru-bottom
places.today: Woods around Montfermeil, east of Paris; much is now built over.

tagline.text: Thicket in the forest near Montfermeil where Boulatruelle finds only a fresh, empty hole.
Glade in the forest of Montfermeil where M. Madeleine's money lay buried for ten years.

places.name: Saint-Paul
places.today: Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis, Rue Saint-Antoine, 4th arrondissement.

tagline.text: Church on the Rue Saint-Antoine whose clock sounds over the Marais.
Church where Marius and Cosette are married.

places.name: The Pont-aux-Choux
places.today: The Rue du Pont-aux-Choux meets the Boulevard des Filles-du-Calvaire here.

tagline.text: Little street off the boulevard by the Marais, where Gavroche finds only a pastrycook's open.
Where the wedding carriages stop beside a cartload of maskers.

places.name: The Blancs-Manteaux
places.today: Notre-Dame-des-Blancs-Manteaux, Rue des Blancs-Manteaux, 4th arrondissement.

tagline.text: Church and street in the Marais.
Point beyond which the old man in black no longer walks.
